close_reason: Public-API change: SetResponse fields from Option<HashMap> to HashMap with #[serde(default)]. Pattern-matching changes for downstream callers. Coordinate with bd:JMAP-6by7 (0.2.0 typed-Id epic) since both are 0.2.0 *-client API cleanup. Deferred.
description:
src/methods/mod.rs:69-79: SetResponse has `created: Option<HashMap<String, T>>`, `updated: Option<...>`, `destroyed: Option<Vec<Id>>`, etc.

RFC 8620 §5.3 says these fields are present and may be empty when nothing was created/updated/destroyed. The wire format does not require them to be omitted on no-op. The current Option<...> shape leaks server inconsistency to the caller — some servers send `"created": null`, some send `"created": {}`, and the type does not distinguish.

For the typical caller, the type they want is `HashMap<...>` (possibly empty). For the meta-caller who cares whether the server sent the field at all, `#[serde(default)]` would let them get `HashMap` and never see None.

Suggested fix:
```
#[serde(default = "HashMap::new")]
pub created: HashMap<String, T>,
```

Three benefits: (1) callers stop pattern-matching Some/None for empty results, (2) types align with RFC's prose model, (3) deserialization tolerates servers that omit empty fields without forcing the caller to handle it.

This applies equally to ChangesResponse — `created: Vec<Id>` is correct, but RFC 8620 §5.2 doesn't let it be None. SetResponse's Option chain is over-defensive and propagates outward.
title: SetResponse fields default to None — caller cannot distinguish 'created absent' vs 'no creates'
